candidates.content_text:
Company Description
Work with Us. Change the World.
At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.
There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
Play a key role in delivering a diverse range of exciting infrastructure projects across roads, commercial and industrial developments, sports, resources, water infrastructure, defence and renewable energy.
You’ll be responsible for developing high-quality civil design models, drawings and technical documentation across projects ranging from local roads and parklands to mine sites, dams, substations, BESS facilities, solar farms and wind farms.
What you'll be doing
- Develop detailed civil design models using 12d Model, including earthworks, roadworks, surface grading, DDA pedestrian access, pavements, drainage networks, culverts and open channels.
- Deliver designs across water and sewer infrastructure, including pipelines, water and sewer reticulation and pump stations, as well as stormwater and bio-retention systems.
- Produce high-quality drawings and documentation using AutoCAD, aligned with client requirements, industry standards and relevant government and regulatory requirements.
- Undertake geometry assessments and swept-path analysis to ensure designs are practical, safe and fit for purpose.
- Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary project teams, coordinating civil interfaces with architectural, structural, landscape, hydraulic, geotechnical, mechanical, electrical, communications, process and environmental disciplines.
- Contribute to design and model reviews, clash detection and safety-in-design activities, ensuring quality is embedded throughout the design process.
- Prepare and review technical inputs for Bills of Quantities, balancing safety, constructability, operational requirements and cost efficiency.
- Work directly with regional project teams to understand requirements, resolve technical queries and deliver work packages to agreed scope, programme and budget.
- Support quality assurance by checking your own work and, where appropriate, reviewing the work of less experienced team members in line with AECOM's quality procedures.
- Contribute to the ongoing improvement of our civil design capability through standard details, design libraries, digital workflows, lessons learned and continuous improvement initiatives.
Qualifications
What you'll bring
We’re looking for someone with a background in civil design and drafting who is keen to contribute to diverse, multidisciplinary projects. You don’t need to tick every box, if you have the right experience and attitude, we’d love to hear from you.
- Civil Engineering qualification (Associate Degree, Diploma, Advanced Diploma or Degree).
- 2+ years’ civil design and drafting experience, ideally across urban, rural, commercial, residential, industrial or mining projects.
- Strong experience in road geometry, pavements, earthworks, grading and drainage design.
- Advanced AutoCAD skills, with experience in 12d Model and vehicle tracking.
- Experience developing civil drawings, models and quantity take-offs.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, including working with multidisciplinary and international teams.
- Experience with water and sewer infrastructure, including reticulation, pump stations, rising mains, pipelines and reservoirs, is highly regarded.
- Familiarity with relevant Australian standards and guidelines, including Austroads, QUDM, WSAA and IPWEA, is desirable.
- Experience taking designs from concept through to construction documentation, as well as working within multidisciplinary model review environments.
- Experience mentoring junior or cadet drafters and contributing to design capability development is advantageous.
You must be an Australian citizen and be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Baseline security clearance.

Who we are
The City of Salisbury is the most progressive council in South Australia, driving growth, jobs, housing and opportunity in the north. With a workforce of over 400 people, we offer the chance to collaborate with teams across the organisation to deliver meaningful, community-focused projects.
The City Infrastructure Department delivers asset management, capital works, and maintenance programs, as well as oversees lease management for local community and sporting clubs, and security and civil compliance functions.
Join us and see the positive impact your work can make.
About the role
The City of Salisbury is seeking three experienced Asset Engineers to join the Engineering Assets & Systems team within City Infrastructure. Opportunities are available across Civil, Roads and Drainage asset portfolios.
Reporting to the Divisional Head, Engineering Assets & Systems (Asset Engineer - Civil and Asset Engineer - Roads) or the Senior Stormwater Engineer (Asset Engineer - Drainage), you will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving asset management plans, undertaking engineering investigations and modelling, and supporting long-term infrastructure planning and investment decisions.
You will play a key role in managing and improving some of the City's most important infrastructure assets, including roads, drainage networks, wetlands, bridges, boardwalks, coastal assets, carparks, signage and stormwater infrastructure, helping ensure they continue to meet the needs of our growing community.
Your key responsibilities will include
- Develop, maintain and improve Asset Management Plans across a range of infrastructure asset classes.
- Undertake engineering investigations, modelling, analysis and reporting to support asset management decisions.
- Develop capital renewal, maintenance and lifecycle programs.
- Assess asset condition, risk, service levels and long-term investment priorities.
- Prepare project briefs and business cases for infrastructure projects and renewal programs.
- Evaluate consultant reports, designs and technical proposals.
- Provide specialist engineering and asset management advice across the organisation.
- Support planning for future growth and infrastructure needs across the city.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community members, developers, government agencies, service authorities and internal stakeholders.
- Communicate technical information and asset management recommendations clearly to a diverse range of stakeholders, including residents, elected members and senior leaders.
- Respond to enquiries from residents, elected members and other stakeholders.
About you
You are a qualified engineer with experience in infrastructure asset management and a passion for delivering practical, long-term outcomes for communities. You combine strong technical capability with excellent communication skills and can confidently engage with a wide range of stakeholders. You are able to translate complex engineering and asset management information into clear, practical advice that supports informed decision-making.
You will also have
- Degree qualifications in Civil Engineering, equivalent qualifications, or proven extensive experience in asset management relating to civil infrastructure and stormwater.
- Experience in infrastructure asset management, planning and lifecycle analysis.
- Knowledge of asset management frameworks such as ISO 55000 and IIMM/IPWEA practices.
- Experience using asset management, GIS and engineering modelling systems.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Proven experience building productive relationships with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong written communication skills, including the preparation of reports, business cases and technical documentation.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Current driver's licence.
Desirable
- Postgraduate qualifications in asset management.
- Experience working within local government.
What we offer
- State-of-the-art Salisbury Community Hub is 25 minutes from the CBD with excellent rail and road connections.
- Modern and positive work environments.
- Free car parking.
- Flexible work options.
- Three additional leave days per year.
- Annual pay rises.
- Health and wellbeing programs, including skin checks, health assessments, flu vaccinations and an employee assistance program.
- Professional development opportunities.

Eligibility

We are committed to creating a safe, inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people with disability, veterans, and members of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Egis is a leading global organisation in architecture, consulting, construction engineering, operations and mobility services. We partner with clients to design, deliver and operate smarter infrastructure and places that respond to the world’s evolving needs.
With more than 22,000 employees worldwide, we combine global capability with strong local insight. Our multidisciplinary expertise enables us to deliver innovative, practical and sustainable solutions that help build more balanced, resilient communities.
At Egis, you’ll be part of a business shaping the future of cities, transport, energy and the built environment, creating lasting impact where it matters most.
Job Description
As a Civil Cadet Drafter in our Urban Transport team at Egis, you will learn to prepare civil and transport infrastructure drawings for local government, state agency and private clients across Queensland. Our projects include road upgrades, intersections and roundabouts, active transport and shared pathways, line marking and signage, and the drainage and civil works that go with them. This is an entry-level role for someone who is studying, or about to start studying, and drafting. You will work alongside experienced drafters and engineers who will support your training while you build real project experience.
With your mentor's guidance, you will:
- Prepare civil drawings in AutoCAD for roads, intersections, shared pathways and drainage.
- Draft general arrangement, typical section, line marking, signage and construction detail plans.
- Produce longitudinal sections, cross sections and drainage plans from engineers' designs.
- Incorporate survey information, utility data and design mark-ups into drawings.
- Prepare drawing packages for preliminary, detailed design and Issued for Construction (IFC) stages.
- Update and maintain drawing registers, title blocks, revisions and project documentation.
- Check that drawings meet council and TMR drafting standards, Austroads, Australian Standards and Egis drafting procedures.
- Support engineers and project managers with design revisions and project documentation.
- Attend site visits and inspections with the team to understand how designs are built.
- Take part in team meetings, training and the development of our drafting standards and templates
Qualifications
No previous drafting experience is required. We welcome applications from students currently enrolled in, or about to start, a Certificate, Diploma or Degree in drafting, civil engineering or a related discipline. You will also have:
- An interest in roads, transport and civil infrastructure
- Some exposure to AutoCAD, 12d Model, Civil 3D or similar software through study or personal projects, or a willingness to learn
- Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- Good attention to detail and a commitment to producing high-quality work
- Good written and verbal communication skills, and a willingness to ask questions
- Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage your own tasks within a team
- A current Australian driver licence, or working towards one
- Any experience with QGIS, or with council, TMR or construction projects, will be an advantage.

- Competitive remuneration and benefits.
- A structured learning and development framework to align with career progression goals.
- Brisbane and Gold Coast location with flexible working arrangements, including remote working options.
- Novated lease
- An inclusive team culture that celebrates performance and rewards accordingly.
- Paid Primary and Secondary Carer Leave Policy, reflecting our commitment to work-life balance.
- Support structures like our Employee Assistance Program, professional mentoring, and buddy program for new starters.
- Opportunities to work on special interest projects.
- Opportunities to work across government, private and resource sectors.
- Opportunities to travel for work across multiple offices.
- Great cultural environment where teamwork and camaraderie are promoted and valued.
- Supportive leadership based on openness.
Egis is committed to creating an inclusive, creative culture that embraces diversity and flexibility. We offer generous parental leave, support flexible work practices and strive to create an environment where employees can connect, collaborate, grow and succeed.
We are expanding in Australia and New Zealand and are excited for you to join our growing team.

candidates.content_text:
Role Overview
The Residue Storage and Industrial Earthworks Civil Engineering Draftsperson prepares detailed civil engineering drawings, plans, sections, technical schedules, and as-constructed documentation in support of engineers and senior design personnel. The position specialises in residue storage and associated industrial civil infrastructure, including containment embankments and wall lifts, retaining structures and buttresses, earthworks, underdrainage, decant pipework, and underground services. Using approved engineering design information, survey data, and site records, the role translates technical requirements into coordinated construction, tender, excavation-planning, and quality-assurance drawing packages.
Key Responsibilities
1. Planning, Engineering Interpretation, and Preparation
- Review engineering design drawings, specifications, site surveys, existing service records, and work instructions to establish drafting requirements and deliverables.
- Interpret topographic and as-constructed survey data, reduced levels, coordinates, chainages, contours, and existing site conditions for incorporation into civil engineering drawings.
- Establish drawing files, relevant references, layouts, legends, scales, and documentation standards in line with project and company requirements.
2. Specialised Civil Engineering Drafting and Documentation
- Prepare general arrangement plans, detailed layouts, profiles, cross-sections, and construction details for residue storage embankments, retaining-wall lifts, buttresses, ramps, berms, and related civil earthworks.
- Develop detailed underdrainage, drainage, and decant drawings, including HDPE pipe and draincoil alignments, diameters, connection and tie-in details, invert levels, grades, and minimum cover requirements based on approved designs.
- Prepare and revise earthworks drawings showing existing and proposed surfaces, contours, crest levels, batter slopes, grading, cut-and-fill extents, and associated quantity tables.
- Produce excavation and dig-permit services plans showing known underground and above-ground services, proposed work boundaries, service interfaces, and potential conflicts for engineering and site review.
- Prepare setting-out information and supporting schedules, including coordinates, reduced levels, pipe quantities, drawing notes, and section references for construction coordination.
3. Survey Integration, Quality Assurance, and As-Constructed Records
- Use survey and as-constructed information to prepare QA plots, long-sections, and comparative drawings for underdrainage, decant installations, retaining walls, and related civil works.
- Document design levels, surveyed as-constructed levels, grades, and variances in tabulations and drawings for engineer review; identify discrepancies without independently certifying design or construction compliance.
- Incorporate redlines, approved design updates, and review comments, and maintain drawing accuracy, traceability, and issue status.
4. Technical Coordination, Quality Control, and File Management
- Coordinate drawing interfaces among earthworks, liner boundaries, access roads, pipelines, civil services, and adjacent infrastructure; flag potential conflicts or missing information to the responsible engineer or senior drafter.
- Check drawing dimensions, coordinates, annotations, levels, scales, sheets, and cross-references against source information and applicable project specifications.
- Maintain version-controlled CAD files, revision registers, drawing issue records, and supporting technical documentation; liaise with engineers, surveyors, supervisors, and other project personnel.
Technical Systems and Capabilities
- AutoCAD: Detailed civil engineering drafting, layouts, profiles, sections, schedules, and revision management.
- Autodesk Civil 3D: Surface and contour information, grading and earthworks representations, profile/section inputs, and coordinated civil drawing preparation.
- Propeller: Review and interpretation of drone-survey surfaces, terrain information, and site data for drafting and QA support.
- Nearmap: Review of aerial imagery and site context to assist infrastructure identification and drawing coordination.
- Applied Civil Drafting Skills: Interpreting survey coordinates and reduced levels; preparing chainage, grade, invert-level, and as-constructed variance tabulations; identifying services interfaces.
Qualifications and Experience
- Relevant qualification in civil engineering, civil engineering drafting, or a closely related discipline.
- At least one (1) year of relevant post-qualification experience in civil engineering drafting consistent with the role and applicable occupational requirements.
- Practical civil engineering drafting experience using AutoCAD; capability with Civil 3D and interpretation of engineering and survey data.
- Demonstrated ability to prepare detailed civil plans and sections for earthworks, retaining structures, drainage, underground services, or comparable civil infrastructure.
- Understanding of drawing QA, document control, construction interfaces, and the need to work under appropriate engineering direction.
- Experience in residue storage, industrial infrastructure, tailings, or water-management earthworks is highly desirable for assigned projects.
Working Conditions
Predominantly office/CAD-based work, with site visits and coordination at operational industrial locations as required by project needs and applicable inductions.

bullets: Join a landmark NSW wind farm project
Be part of a high-performing team delivering projects that make an impact
Enjoy a DIDO lifestyle, competitive salary and roster flexibility
candidates.content_text:
Zenviron is seeking an experienced Civil Project Engineer to support the delivery of a major Wind Farm project in the Hunter Region, NSW.
This is a unique opportunity to join a market-leading renewable energy contractor and contribute to the delivery of one of Australia's largest clean energy infrastructure projects. Initially based in our Newcastle office, you will support engineering, procurement and planning activities before transitioning to site during the construction phase.
As the Civil Project Engineer, you will play a critical role in coordinating and delivering major civil works packages, ensuring project objectives are achieved safely, efficiently and to the highest quality standards.
Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate the delivery of civil construction works across the project lifecycle.
- Manage civil work packages including bulk earthworks, roads, drainage, foundations, hardstands and underground services.
- Assist with project planning, scheduling and resource coordination to ensure works are delivered to programme.
- Review engineering drawings, specifications and technical documentation to ensure compliance and constructability.
- Coordinate subcontractors and site crews to achieve project milestones safely and efficiently.
- Manage RFIs, design changes, non-conformances and project documentation.
- Support cost control, forecasting and progress reporting activities.
- Monitor construction quality requirements, including inspections, test plans and completion documentation.
- Identify and mitigate construction risks and support problem-solving across site activities.
- Foster a strong culture of safety, quality and continuous improvement.
What You Will Bring
- Degree qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
- Previous experience as a Project Engineer, Civil Project Engineer or Site Engineer delivering civil construction projects.
- Experience with earthworks, drainage, roads, pavements, concrete structures or associated civil infrastructure works.
- Strong understanding of project delivery, construction methodologies and engineering documentation.
- Experience managing subcontractors and coordinating multiple work fronts.
- Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with construction, engineering and commercial teams.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Experience within renewable energy, infrastructure, mining, resources or major construction projects will be highly regarded.
- A practical, solutions-focused approach and willingness to be actively involved in site delivery.
The Opportunity
This position is ideally suited to candidates based in Newcastle, Hunter Valley, Sydney, Dubbo or the Mid North Coast regions. Preference will be given to candidates who can initially work from the Newcastle office before transitioning to site during project delivery.
The project will operate on a DIDO basis, with camp accommodation provided. A competitive remuneration package will be offered, along with roster arrangements designed to maximise time at home.
This is an outstanding opportunity for a Civil Project Engineer looking to gain exposure to a landmark renewable energy project while developing their career within a growing and highly respected EPC contractor.
Why Zenviron?
We are committed to our philosophy of Empowering People and encourage innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement. We embrace the benefits of employing talented people from diverse backgrounds and experiences and encourage applications from all suitably qualified candidates.
At Zenviron, your contribution will be recognised and valued. You'll have the opportunity to work on industry-leading renewable energy projects while developing your career within a growing and respected organisation.
About Us
Zenviron is a joint venture between Monadelphous and ZEM Energy and is a market-leading engineering, procurement and construction contractor specialising in the design and delivery of large-scale renewable energy projects across Australia. Through our expertise in wind, solar and battery energy storage projects, we are helping to power Australia's clean energy future.

candidates.content_text:
Company Description
Egis is a leading global organisation in architecture, consulting, construction engineering, operations and mobility services. We partner with clients to design, deliver and operate smarter infrastructure and places that respond to the world’s evolving needs.
With more than 22,000 employees worldwide, we combine global capability with strong local insight. Our multidisciplinary expertise enables us to deliver innovative, practical and sustainable solutions that help build more balanced, resilient communities.
At Egis, you’ll be part of a business shaping the future of cities, transport, energy and the built environment, creating lasting impact where it matters most.
Job Description
As a Civil Engineer in our Urban Transport team at Egis, you will focus on delivering civil and transport infrastructure design for local government, state agencies and private clients across Queensland, with the opportunity to support and work on projects nationally. Our projects include road upgrades, intersections and roundabouts, active transport and shared pathways, line marking and signage, and the drainage and civil works that go with them. With a strong pipeline of projects in hand, we’re excited to be growing our Queensland team in 2027.
You will be responsible for:
- Delivery and coordination of projects and proposals, with the potential for both office and site-based works.
- Contribute to detailed design plans for roads, intersections, pathways and drainage, working closely with drafters and project managers.
- Coordinate the production and revision of Engineering designs by liaising with internal Design teams and sub-consultants.
- Apply Austroads, Australian Standards, TMR and council standards to deliver safe, compliant and buildable designs.
- Prepare project deliverables, tender documentation, design documentation, technical reports, bills of quantities, cost estimates and specifications to meet client requirements for projects of reasonable complexity.
- Assume responsibility for project planning and management of resources for small projects or parts of larger projects.
- Supporting the well-being, development, and resourcing of team members.
- Participating in client management and business development.
- Playing an active role in the business groups through regular meetings, workshops, training and business planning.
Qualifications
Ideally, you will have 1+ years of experience (we are also open to those graduating in 2026) in a similar role within a consultancy environment servicing local governments across Queensland. In addition, you will also have:
- A degree in Civil Engineering (Engineers Australia accredited or equivalent), and be working towards RPEQ registration
- Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (i.e. Word, Excel, Outlook, Project, etc.), with experience in AutoCAD or QGIS.
- A thorough understanding of general civil engineering and design principles pertaining to roads, intersections, active transport, earthworks, drainage, water management design and general civil works
- Demonstrated experience supporting local and state government projects
- Demonstrated involvement in project management and delivery for small to medium projects across the full life cycle
- Experience in urban road, intersection, active transport or public transport projects highly regarded
- Strong written and verbal communication skills to liaise with stakeholders at all levels
- Strong organisation and problem-solving skills
Additional Information
The Benefits
- Competitive remuneration and benefits.
- A structured learning and development framework to align with career progression goals.
- Brisbane and Gold Coast location with flexible working arrangements, including remote working options.
- Novated lease
- An inclusive team culture that celebrates performance and rewards accordingly.
- Paid Primary and Secondary Carer Leave Policy, reflecting our commitment to work-life balance.
- Support structures like our Employee Assistance Program, professional mentoring, and buddy program for new starters.
- Opportunities to work on special interest projects.
- Opportunities to work across government, private and resource sectors.
- Opportunities to travel for work across multiple offices.
- Great cultural environment where teamwork and camaraderie are promoted and valued.
- Supportive leadership based on openness.
Egis is committed to creating an inclusive, creative culture that embraces diversity and flexibility. We offer generous parental leave, support flexible work practices and strive to create an environment where employees can connect, collaborate, grow and succeed.
We are expanding in Australia and New Zealand and are excited for you to join our growing team.
